follow_ups.artifact_repair: Re-derive duval-replay-material's claims through materialize -- the path where _claim_standing applies the cap -- and re-render, so C-curated lands as EXTENDS with a reason. Recommended over 'let a file-fact keep CONFIRMS' because the replay manifest's own status_reason already reads 'producer is replay: no model mined these candidates; not publication-eligible', which directly contradicts CONFIRMS. Route: copy the docket to scratch, re-run the replay materialisation for lane duval-replay-material through materialize (assemble_docket at materialize.py:2121), diff CLAIMS.md/MANIFEST.json, then copy back. Do NOT hand-edit MANIFEST.json -- the cap must come from the rule, and the new verifier will flag a hand-edit anyway.
follow_ups.vocabulary: CONFIRMS is overloaded: it is used both for 'a model assessed this' and by authors for 'a file at a commit was verified by hashing'. A distinct standing (e.g. VERIFIED-MECHANICAL) for mechanically verified file-facts is the honest long-term fix, but it needs a manifest-schema change and resextract/docket/1 must not be bumped in this unit -- so it was NOT implemented here. Until then the fail-closed cap stands and the verifier flags the contradiction.
